The value is a CPython `ast` node yielded by `ast.walk(ast.parse(condition, mode='eval'))`, where `condition` is the composer/LLM-authored gate expression carried on `NodeSpec.condition` — Tier-3 external input, already shape-screened by `_validate_gate_expression` at the sole caller `_gate_expression_type_diagnostics_for_observed_csv` before this function is reached. The node type is stdlib grammar, NOT an ELSPETH-owned type, so ADR-032's 'nominally type what ELSPETH owns' has no owned class to name here, and the house `type(x) is C` idiom is unavailable on principle: that idiom asserts a CLOSED union, and we do not own `ast` and cannot declare its node hierarchy closed (the module has historically carried subclass-compatible aliases, and `isinstance` is the traversal idiom the stdlib documents). What the guard protects: the walker harvests literal row field names only, and every conjunct in the chain must hold before `node.slice.value` is appended; any other node kind in an arbitrary valid Python expression must fall through silently rather than contribute a bogus field name, because those names drive `_source_field_reaches_connection_without_type_change` and therefore whether a blocking `gate_expression_type_mismatch_against_source_schema` diagnostic is emitted. web/composer/tools/generation.py:R6:_gat: R6 `except ExpressionEvaluationError:` around `parser.evaluate(row)`. The exception is not swallowed — it is reified. The handler appends `_blocking_diagnostic(code='gate_expression_type_mismatch_against_source_schema', ...)` to the `diagnostics` accumulator that is this function's return value, then `break`s out of the sampled-row loop so one gate reports once. The controls, by symbol: `_blocking_diagnostic` raises `AssertionError` unless the code is registered in `_BLOCKING_DIAGNOSTIC_CODES`, so the outcome cannot silently become an unrecognised code; the caller `_compute_proof_diagnostics_for_source` merges the returned list into the proof diagnostics that `compute_proof_diagnostics` returns, which `preview_pipeline` and `validate_state` render as blocking. This is the rule's known blind spot for the validator-accumulator shape: `_handler_is_silent` counts only `raise`/`return`/`yield` as explicit outcomes. Tier: the raise originates in `ExpressionParser.evaluate(row)` where `row` came from `_sample_csv_rows` over an operator-uploaded CSV blob — Tier-3 observed content. The exception text is deliberately NOT propagated or quoted (the emitted message says so): the evaluator's error can quote sampled row values and the observed field/key set, and this tool's output reaches the composer LLM. Re-raising would abort the whole bounded proof for every other source because one authored gate is mistyped, which is the opposite of what a preview/repair loop must do.

R6 `except MemoryError:` beside the `ExpressionEvaluationError` handler on the same `parser.evaluate(row)` call. Not a swallow: the handler appends `_blocking_diagnostic(code='gate_expression_preview_memory_exhaustion', ...)` to the same `diagnostics` accumulator and `break`s. The actual resource bound is the control ahead of it, by symbol: `ExpressionParser.has_string_amplification_risk` diagnoses `gate_expression_unbounded_string_amplification` IN PLACE OF evaluating, so a str-repetition / printf-formatting expression over an observed (string-typed) field never reaches `evaluate` at all. This handler exists so that if that predicate is ever outrun, the resulting resource event is reported as a resource failure and does NOT receive the schema-typing repair text that the sibling handler emits — a misrouted repair would tell the operator to declare a numeric field for a problem that is not a typing mismatch. Tier-3 observed CSV content, bounded by `_sample_csv_rows` (8 KiB / 100 rows). Letting `MemoryError` escape would take down the whole `preview_pipeline` tool in the web process at the moment it is already degraded; the diagnostic is explicitly best-effort and the comment at the site says so.
web/composer/tools/generation.py:R6:_com: R6 `except ValueError as exc:` around `get_raw_schema_config(source.options, owner=f'source:{source.plugin}')`. This is a genuine Tier-3 boundary, not a Tier-1 audit-data violation. `source.options` is composer/operator-authored configuration re-read from persisted session state: ELSPETH authored the container (`SourceSpec` and its options mapping) and the schema that validated it at write time, but the VALUES were authored by the operator or the composer LLM, and persistence does not promote them to Tier-1 — the store is mutable (hand-edits, stale restore) and the validating contract can drift between write and read, so re-reading here is a FRESH Tier-3 boundary. A `ValueError` from `get_raw_schema_config` is therefore recoverable bad external-origin input, exactly like a malformed source row. It is not ignored: the handler appends `_csv_source_schema_config_error_diagnostic(blob_id=..., facts=..., exc=exc)` — which carries `type(exc).__name__` while redacting raw values — and then rebinds `schema_config = None`, so the `if schema_config is not None` guard immediately below skips every dependent schema-mismatch analysis for this blob. That is the quarantine-equivalent control, by symbol: record what we found, skip the dependent work, keep the other blob sources' proofs. Future drift that dropped the diagnostic append, dropped `exc=exc`, or stopped rebinding `schema_config` to `None` would invalidate this suppression.

R6 `except ValueError as exc:` around `_csv_source_field_mapping(source.options)`. Same Tier-3 boundary as the `get_raw_schema_config` handler above: `source.options` is composer/operator-authored configuration re-read from persisted session state, so a malformed `field_mapping` is recoverable bad external-origin input, not a broken ELSPETH invariant. The exception is reified, not swallowed: the handler appends `_csv_source_field_resolution_error_diagnostic(blob_id=..., facts=..., exc=exc)` and sets `field_resolution_failed = True`. `field_resolution_failed` is the control, by symbol — it gates `derive_required_header_mismatch_risk` and the `schema_config.mode == 'fixed'` branch that calls `derive_extra_column_risk`, so no header/column analysis runs against a field mapping we could not resolve and no false `csv_source_blob_header_mismatch` or `csv_fixed_schema_omits_observed_columns` blocker is emitted. `_csv_source_field_resolution_error_diagnostic` emits a blocking `csv_source_field_resolution_error` carrying `error_class: type(exc).__name__` while redacting observed headers and the raw error, because malformed/headerless CSV can expose row content to the composer LLM. Escaping would crash the whole `preview_pipeline` tool on one bad option value.

R6 `except ValueError as exc:` around `derive_required_header_mismatch_risk(facts, declared, explicit_required_fields=..., field_mapping=...)`. The inputs are Tier-3 on both sides: `declared`/`explicit_required_fields` come from the composer/operator-authored `source.options` schema block (re-read from mutable session state — a fresh Tier-3 boundary, not a Tier-1 invariant), and `facts.observed_headers` are parsed from an operator-uploaded CSV blob. A `ValueError` here is a rejection of that external input by the risk deriver, not a broken ELSPETH invariant. It is reified exactly like the `_csv_source_field_mapping` handler: append `_csv_source_field_resolution_error_diagnostic(..., exc=exc)` (blocking `csv_source_field_resolution_error`, `error_class` only, headers redacted) and set `field_resolution_failed = True`. `field_resolution_failed` is the control, by symbol: it leaves `missing_declared` at its `()` initialiser and gates the `elif schema_config.mode == 'fixed' and not field_resolution_failed` branch, so no downstream mismatch verdict is derived from an analysis that did not complete. Future drift that dropped the append or stopped setting `field_resolution_failed` would invalidate this suppression.

R6 `except ValueError as exc:` around `derive_extra_column_risk(facts, declared, field_mapping=...)` in the `schema_config.mode == 'fixed'` arm. Same Tier-3 pairing as the `derive_required_header_mismatch_risk` handler: composer/operator-authored declared fields and field mapping re-read from persisted session state, compared against headers observed in an operator-uploaded blob. The handler appends `_csv_source_field_resolution_error_diagnostic(..., exc=exc)` — blocking `csv_source_field_resolution_error`, `error_class` only, observed headers redacted — and does not re-raise. The control here is the binding, by symbol: `missing` is initialised to `()` before the `try`, so a failed derivation leaves it empty and the guard `if missing and source.on_validation_failure == 'discard'` immediately below cannot emit a `csv_fixed_schema_omits_observed_columns` blocker off an analysis that never completed. Reporting the failure and declining to assert the dependent verdict is the correct disposition for a preview/repair loop; re-raising would abort the bounded proof for every other blob-backed source in the pipeline.
web/composer/tools/generation.py:R5:_att: R5 `if not isinstance(evidence, Mapping): raise RuntimeError(...)` in `_attribute_proof_diagnostic_to_source`. The value is Tier-1 — diagnostics this module constructs — so this is a contract self-check that crashes on anomaly, which is what the manifesto requires at Tier-1; the finding is about the discriminator, not the disposition. `isinstance` against the `Mapping` ABC is retained deliberately, and neither alternative is honest here. Narrowing to `type(evidence) is not dict` would CONTRADICT this module's own declared contract: `_blocking_diagnostic` and `_warning_diagnostic` both declare the parameter as `evidence_locator: Mapping[str, Any]`, and because the else-branch raises, that narrowing would convert a legitimate non-dict Mapping into a `RuntimeError` at runtime. Dropping the check is equally unavailable: the value's static type is `Any` (it is `diagnostic['evidence_locator']` off a `Mapping[str, Any]`), and not every producer flows through `_blocking_diagnostic`. `_compute_proof_diagnostics_for_source` builds its `source_inspection_warning` mirror as a bare dict literal that is never type-checked as `_BlockingDiagnosticPayload`, and this function's own return is a third raw-literal shape, so there is no owned type to name as the control that would guarantee the shape at this call site. `Mapping` is therefore the widest runtime discriminator consistent with the declared producer signatures, and the guard exists so a producer that emitted a non-mapping locator fails loudly here rather than shipping `{**evidence, 'source_name': ...}` garbage into the proof diagnostics the composer LLM reads. The honest removal is to make the diagnostic payload an owned type end-to-end, which is a separate change to every producer in this module.
web/composer/tools/generation.py:R6:comp: R6 `except ValueError:` around `UUID(resolved_blob_id)` in `_memoized_resolver`. Nothing is swallowed: this is a try/except/else parse whose BOTH arms bind the same variable to an explicit value, and the rule fires only because `_handler_is_silent` does not count an assignment as an explicit outcome. `resolved_blob_id` is Tier-3 — it originates in `source.options['blob_ref']`, composer/operator-authored configuration re-read from persisted session state — so a non-UUID value is legitimate external input, not an ELSPETH invariant violation, and there is nothing to report: readiness and custody are decided downstream by `uncached_resolver` and by `_compute_proof_diagnostics_for_source`, which emits `source_inspection_failed` when resolution fails. The handler's binding IS the control, by symbol: `cache_key = ('raw', resolved_blob_id)` places unparseable ids in a namespace distinct from the `'uuid'` and `'noncanonical'` namespaces the `else:` arm builds, so a malformed blob_ref can never collide with a canonical UUID key in `resolved_by_blob_id` and cannot cause one source's custody resolution to be served to another. Raising instead would make one bad `blob_ref` abort the entire bounded proof; a bare `str` cache key without the namespace tag would reintroduce exactly the collision this arm prevents.
